properties.NAME: Southwood
properties.PROFILE_2018: Originally known as Southwood Park, this community stands on land which, prior to being expropriated in 1940 to make way for the DIL plant, included the Stanley Farm, the Campbell Brothers farm and the McCausland farm. Construction of this 138 acre residential site began in July of 1960. The Perini Company, who were the general contractors under the name of Duffins Creek Estates Ltd. were responsible for constructing the roads, sidewalks, sewers and water mains but private builders were responsible for the construction of the actual homes which numbered in excess of 400.

properties.NAME: Riverside
properties.PROFILE_2018: Located just north-west of Pickering Village, the Riverside Community no doubt gets its name from Riverside Farm which was located in this area. This farmland was once the site of the Woodruff Tavern which was built in 1808 by Noadiah Woodruff on Lot 17, Concession 2. In 1852 William and Phoebe Hartrick built the Hartick Farm House for their son, William Tetes Hartrick. This 200 acre farm was located in the northern part of the Riverside community near Church Street and Rossland Road. The house, which is now known as the Ajax Kinsmen Heritage Centre, and some of the surrounding land is now owned by the Town of Ajax and used as a banquet and meeting facility.

properties.NAME: Downtown
properties.PROFILE_2018:
In the late 1940s, the concept of the first planned commercial/industrial community in Ontario was formalized. The original plans for Ajax included establishing the residential development on the east side of Harwood Avenue, with the commercial/industrial businesses on the west side. This was further defined by the boulevard dividing Harwood Avenue. The creation of a “downtown” area for the new community was started with the construction of the Ajax Plaza, which opened in 1951. This was one of the first strip plazas built in Canada.

The original DIL hospital was moved to vacant land on the west side of Harwood Avenue, north of Clements Road in 1953 and the Ajax/Pickering Hospital was created. The first Ajax Community Centre was built to the north of the hospital in 1967. The last part of the “downtown” development was the construction of the Harwood Place Mall on the northwest corner of Harwood Avenue and Bayly Street, which opened in 1970.

properties.NAME: Audley North
properties.PROFILE_2018: The first settler of the Audley area was Scotsman Alex Dunlop who purchased land near Audley and Taunton Roads in 1835.  Originally known it was known as Brown’s Corners after Abraham Brown, who owned the first hotel and bar. Renamed Audley in 1858, the settlement had become a self-sufficient village with services such as a blacksmith, shoe repair shop, butcher shop, wagon and paint shop, tannery, general store, post office, hotel and a school in the 1960s. .To accommodate the growing population, a succession of schoolhouses were built: the first Audley Public School was a one-room log building erected 1840 and the last schoolhouse was a three-room brick structure erected in 1964. While the bustling hamlet of Audley is no longer, the area continues to thrive within the Town of Ajax with new housing and recreation facilities, including the Audley Recreation Centre which opened in 2013.

properties.NAME: Salem Business Area
properties.PROFILE_2018: With prime exposure along Highway 401, the Salem Business Area consists of prestige employment lands. This area is intended as an employment-intensive, pedestrian-friendly employment gateway. Development within this area exhibits a high standard of building design and landscaping. Current uses include hotels, a convention centre, athletic club and luxury automobile dealerships. The southeastern portion consists of environmentally protected lands within the Carruthers Creek watershed.

properties.NAME: Salem Heights
properties.PROFILE_2018: The community of Salem Heights is situated on land that, back in 1877, was owned by the Puckrins, the Chapmans and the McQuays.  Bordered by the Canadian Pacific Railway, Carruthers Creek and the Greenbelt, Salem Heights is located at the northern limits of the Town’s urban area. The neighbourhood is predominantly residential, containing a mix of single detached, semi-detached, and townhouses. Small commercial plazas located along the northern boundary of the neighbourhood provide residents with convenient access to retail and personal service shops. A series of neighbourhood parks and parkettes offer recreational and outdoor amenity space throughout the area.

properties.NAME: Duffins Bay
properties.PROFILE_2018: Prior to 1940, this community sat on land which was part of the Down Farm. In 1940, the land was expropriated by the Canadian Government in order to build the Defense Industries Limited Munitions Plant. The storage sheds for the completed rounds of ammunition were located in this area. After the war and the dismantling of DIL, the area was designated for residential occupation according to the plans which had been developed by the Canada  Mortgage and Housing Corporation (CMHC) whose aim it was to turn Ajax into a fully planned model town. In 1973 Wimpey Homes Ltd. began construction on over 800 single family dwellings and townhouses. At the time it was one of the largest projects even undertaken by the company.

properties.NAME: Audley Road Business Area
properties.PROFILE_2018: The Audley Road Business Area offers a unique mix of employment opportunities. Located immediately south of Highway 401 are employment lands which contain a large warehouse/distribution centre. Kingston Road, a regional corridor, runs directly through the business area. Both the north and south side are identified as a potential area for the development of an entertainment and recreation node. Currently, located on the north side of Kingston Road, is Ajax Downs, a gaming and gambling establishment which serves as a major regional tourism attraction. The western portion consists of environmentally sensitive lands within the Carruthers Creek watershed.

properties.NAME: Westney Heights
properties.PROFILE_2018: The Westney Heights community is located in an area which was largely farmland during the 19th and early part of the 20th century. In 1877 landowners included J. Dale, R. Miller and J. Baxter. The house, located at 368 Kingston Road W, was built in the 1880s, on land which was purchased by Alexander Margach in 1866. The land remained a part of the Margach estate until 1916. In the late 1970s and early ‘80s JDS Investments Ltd. undertook a project to build over 1,700 homes in this community which would bring a significant increase to the population of Ajax.

properties.NAME: Carruthers Creek Business Area
properties.PROFILE_2018: The southern portion of the area is currently home to a variety of large retail plazas and is seen as a regional commercial centre. As the Town identifies this area as the Uptown Regional Centre, this area is envisioned as a place to live, work and play consisting of intensified mixed use developments. The northern portion consists of a variety of employment lands. Situated along local and regional corridors, this area has the potential to be a major employment area within the Town.

properties.NAME: Midtown
properties.PROFILE_2018: The Midtown Community contains some of the oldest heritage properties in Ajax. The Old Post Inn, located on Highway 2, just across from Picov Downs, is the oldest building in Ajax. Built in 1815 by George Washington Post, it was used as a stagecoach inn for travellers between Toronto and Kingston.  This community is also the site of the wartime housing which was built for the families of the employees of Defense Industries Limited. George Finley, working for the Central Mortgage and Housing Corporation (CMHC), was the administrator of the project which saw the construction of 600 prefabricated homes just north of Highway 2. These homes were meant to be temporary and the rumour was that, following the end of the war, they were to be shipped to Britain to provide temporary shelter for those who had lost their homes due to German bombs. A group of tenants, outraged that they would have to leave their homes and the community that they had created, petitioned Queens Park to allow them to stay. The government agreed and the residents were offered the chance to buy their homes with prices ranging between $2500 and $3300.

properties.NAME: Central Employment Area
properties.PROFILE_2018: The Central Employment Area lies just south of Highway 401 and is bordered by Church Street to the west, Monarch Avenue to the east and Westney Road to the south. Prior to the expropriation of land by the Canadian Government in 1940, the land was occupied by farms belonging to E.L. Ruddy, John Wilson, Richard Appleton, W. Linton and the Miller Brothers. During the Defense Industries Limited days, some of the production lines were located here along with the large warehouse buildings where trains were loaded with completed rounds of ammunition, ready to be shipped overseas to aid our allies. Once the war was over, the DIL plant was closed down and the land was turned over to Central Mortgage and Housing Corporation. It was they who saw the potential to turn Ajax into a model planned community. George W. Finley, nicknamed the Father of Ajax, was given the task of attracting industry to this fledgling community. Fortunately, thanks to the infrastructure left behind from the DIL plant including the steam plant, the water plant, the sewage plant, the railway lines and several buildings, Mr. Finley was able to persuade several British industrial firms to establish Canadian branches here. In 1950 Slough Estates purchased a block of the industrial lands and began building rental premises for industrial use. This attracted several Canadian businesses and American firms looking to open branch sites in Canada. Some of the first industries in Ajax included Ajax Magnethermic Canada, Atlas Tag Company of Canada, Bayley Engineering Limited, Cametoid Limited, Chrysler Canada Limtied, Dowty Equipment of Canada Limited, Dupont Canada Inc., Monarch Knitting, Pye Canada Ltd., Sandra Tea & Coffee Limited and Stark Electronics Ltd.

properties.NAME: Clover Ridge
properties.PROFILE_2018: The community of Clover Ridge sits on land that, prior to 1940, was occupied by the J. Devine and McCausland Brothers farms. Following the practice of naming streets after the veterans from the HMS Ajax, the area is named in honour of Ron Clover. Bordered by Dreyer Road to the north, Lake Ontario to the south, Harwood Avenue to the west and Pickering Beach Road to the east, the subdivision was developed by Wimpey Homes Limited in two phases, beginning in 1968. It added more than 500 homes to Ajax and was thought to have the potential to increase the Town’s population by 25%.

properties.NAME: Duffin's Crossing
properties.PROFILE_2018:
The Duffin’s Crossing community is situated on land which, back in 1877, once belonged to such families as the Dales, the Hartricks, the Boones and the Vartys. A portion of Oliver Badgerow’s farm is also located here. A member of the infamous Markham Gang, his grave is located within the Greenwood Conservation Area.

This area is envisioned to accommodate a mix of development within the near future. With current residential and mixed commercial corridor designations, it has the potential to include a variety of low density to high density residential development as well as a mix of retail, office and service commercial uses. The northern portion of this area is within the boundaries of the Greenbelt and will continue to keep its rural nature. Due to its location within the Duffin’s Creek watershed, there is considerable amount of environmentally protected lands throughout the area.

properties.NAME: Meadow Ridge
properties.PROFILE_2018: This area was designed to have an upscale orientation consisting primarily of low density housing directed towards the upper end of the housing market. Townhouse and seniors units located along the south boundary of the neighbourhood provide for a mix of housing while a variety of retail and service commercial uses are clustered along the northern edge of the neighbourhood. Environmentally protected lands surrounding Duffins Creek separate the rest of the area from future residential developments incorporating a variety of housing types. A proposed multi-use trail system along the Hydro Corridor will provide pedestrian connectivity within the area.

properties.NAME: Memorial Village
properties.PROFILE_2018:
Ajax underwent several transformations from 1941 to 1949. The closure of Defence Industries Limited, the shell filling plant in operation from 1941 - 1945, left an abandoned war plant, roads, railways, a steam system connected by miles of pipe lines to the industrial buildings, a water pumping station and sewage disposal plant. The site was leased to the University of Toronto and the vacant buildings were used to create the Ajax Campus for engineering studies, in use from 1946 to 1949. The crown corporation, Central Mortgage and Housing Corporation (CMHC), had assumed control of the site with the understanding that Ajax would not remain a “Government Town”. With a mandate to develop one of the first “planned community”, preliminary studies were done in 1948 to determine the most effective means of establishing a full municipal government as soon as it became feasible to do so. Shortly after, the first Zoning By-law was drafted, enabling the CMHC to create the first residential subdivision in the newly established community of Ajax.

Neighbourhood One, as it was referred to, provided the architect a unique opportunity for the groupings of buildings in unconventional patterns, and new ideas were welcomed, including the philosophy that no home in new Ajax would be more than 200 yards from a park or greenbelt. The neighbourhood has seen little change outside of home improvements including additions, exterior alterations, front porches, shed and detached garages to the single detached dwellings.

properties.NAME: Discovery Bay
properties.PROFILE_2018: The first documented European settler in the area, William Peak, purchased land at the mouth of Duffin’s Creek around 1800. Many of this family is buried in the Peak/Greenlaw Cemetery located on the west bank of the creek. On the east side of the creek the Field family had purchased land and settled there to farm.  Part of the farm is now known as Rotary Park, established in 1951. In the early years the park offered camping near the lake. A small frame building which had once belonged to the Field Family was used as a concession stand with the revenue going towards the upkeep of the park. The name, Discovery Bay, was given to this area by the developer.

properties.NAME: Applecroft
properties.PROFILE_2018: This is a well-established predominantly low density residential neighbourhood with a southern portion consisting of commercial uses and higher density residential uses along Kingston Road. Neighbourhood centres located along Westney Road and Harwood Avenue provide shopping opportunities for the surrounding residents while a variety of neighbourhood parks and a multi-use trail system offer recreational opportunities. Various medium density developments containing townhouses are also located throughout the area.

properties.NAME: The recorded history of Pickering Villages starts with the first known European settler, an Irishman
properties.PROFILE_2018:
The recorded history of Pickering Villages starts with the first known European settler, an Irishman by the name of Duffin. When the Crown Surveyor was sent out in 1791 to create a series of townships in the newly formed Upper Canada, no trace of Duffin could be found other than his cabin on the east shore of the stream, which the surveyor marked as Duffin’s Creek on his map. Settlement began in 1807, when Timothy Rogers purchased 800 acres of land around the creek, bringing 20 Quaker families, as well as his own, creating a new community referred to as “Duffin’s Creek”. Kingston Road, which ran through the village, was completed in 1817.  As the only easterly route from Toronto and Kingston it served as a post road for stagecoaches delivering mail, it became the site for numerous inns to accommodate the stagecoaches and travelers. Pickering, as it became known as around the 1850's, thrived through the late 1800s and would elevated to a Police Village in 1900, hence after called Pickering Village.

With the completion of the Grand Trunk Railway in 1856, Pickering Village was an important grist-milling and local commercial centre. In 1974, the Region of Durham was created where Pickering Village was annexed to the Town of Ajax. Since 1993, the Pickering Village Business Improvement Area was formed to serve the local businesses. Today, Pickering Village consists of a number of restaurants, retail businesses and professional services.

properties.NAME: Audley South
properties.PROFILE_2018: The Audley South Community has a rich history, featuring some of the most prominent families in Pickering Township and the Durham Region. The Brown family, who were one of the Quaker families brought to the area by Timothy Rogers in the early 19th century, owned several acres of land in this area. The cottage at 744 Kingston Road E sits on property which was owned by the Browns from 1820-1868. It was part of what would become the Stonehaven Estate. The land was later purchased by R.J. Flemming, who tuned 100 acres into apple orchards and sold them under the name Pickering Farms. In 1927, George McLaughlin, older brother and business partner of Robert Samuel McLaughlin, first president of General Motors in Oshawa, purchased the land and had Stonehaven built for his daughter, Ethel, and son-in-law, Norman Irwin. The orchards attached to the estate were renamed Red Wing Orchards in a nod to Mr. Irwin who was a pilot known for flying a plane with red wings. The estate remained in the family until 1985 when it was sold to Charles Coppa, the owner of Highland Farms. The O’Connor Farm house at 762 Rossland Road E was built by Denis O’Connor in 1845. His son, Denis, went on to become the Archbishop of Toronto in 1899. Archbishop Denis O’Connor Catholic High School is named in his honour. The O’Connor property has been recognized as a century farm, having been operated by the same family for more than 100 years.

properties.NAME: Pickering Beach
properties.PROFILE_2018: In the 1920s, James Tuckett came to the shores of Lake Ontario with a vision to create the ideal summer resort. Tuckett christened this new destination Pickering Beach. He built a number of cabins and hired Stanley Mann as the resort’s real estate agent. Tuckett soon saw his vision of a bustling summer resort come to fruition, as the site became a vacation destination for upscale Toronto families such as the Corbets, the Eatons, and the Loblaws. As weekend travel became quite popular with the advent of the automobile, the community continued to evolve: the Pickering Beach Community Association was formed in the 1930s and Paradise School was opened in 1955. Upon the creation of Durham Region in 1974, Pickering Beach was included in the land transfer package and became part of the Town of Ajax.

properties.NAME: Deer Creek
properties.PROFILE_2018: This area was named by the developer who built the Deer Creek Golf and Country Club in the late 1980s. Squire Drive was named in honour of the family who had owned and farmed much of the land now occupied by the golf course, where they had resided for many generations.

properties.NAME: Carruthers Creek
properties.PROFILE_2018: In 1877 much of the land which makes up the Carruthers Creek community was owned by such families as the Richardsons, Remmers, Orvis’, McCauslands and Browns.

properties.NAME: Nottingham
properties.PROFILE_2018: The Nottingham Community is built on land which was once the Westney Farm. The farm house, located at 1733 Westney Road North, was built in 1856 by Thomas Elliott. Designated under the Ontario Heritage Act, it is an excellent example of nineteenth century rural architecture. The property was purchased in 1892 by Stephen Westney. In 1929, William Heron Westney, his son, renamed the property Westglen which was a combination of the last names of himself and his wife, Janet Glendinning. William Westney was very active in local affairs and in 1951, in honour of his service to the community, the road which runs past the farm was named Westney Road.

properties.NAME: Lakeside
properties.PROFILE_2018: In 1877, the land upon which the community of Lakeside currently stands was occupied by farms belonging to the Richardson family. Located at the southeast corner of the Town, the western half includes the southeastern limits of the Town’s urban boundary while the eastern half is within the boundaries of the Greenbelt. The western half includes more recent residential subdivisions containing both single detached and townhouse dwellings. To the east, rural and environmentally protected lands including the Warbler Swamp which are included within the Greenbelt. Ontoro Boulevard, located at the southern edge, features a variety of waterfront homes along the shore of Lake Ontario. A multi-use trail system extending from the southern to northern limits of the neighbourhood separates the urban development from the protected lands.

properties.NAME: Hermitage
properties.PROFILE_2018:
Pickering College, a boarding school, was built by the Religious Society of Friends (Quakers) in 1878 north of Kingston Road and east of Church Street in Pickering Village. An imposing four story red brick building surrounded by 10 acres of land and situated on the highest point in the Village, it accommodated 100 students preparing for entrance into the universities and the professions of the day. Reputed to be one of the major places of learning in the country, it attracted students’ world-wide, including those from Japan, Europe and Australia. In 1899, Samuel Rogers donated the funds to build a gymnasium for the school. The main building was destroyed by fire during the Christmas holidays of 1906 and the decision was made to move and rebuild Pickering College in Newmarket. The undamaged gymnasium was purchased by E. L. Ruddy and converted it into a summer home named the Hermitage. The property was abandoned around 1960, and lost to a fire in 1987.

The Hermitage building was an important representation of Greek Revival Style institutional architecture from the turn of the century. Since then, a subdivision was developed by a builder, Runnymede on the land surrounding the site. Hermitage Community Park was also built on the site within the subdivision on Griffiths Street in recognition of the significance of the property. A replica of the artesian well that once occupied the site can be found in the park.

properties.NAME: South Greenwood
properties.PROFILE_2018: The Community of South Greenwood gets its name from the hamlet of Greenwood, located just a couple of concessions north of the community. Formerly known as Norwood, it was renamed in 1852 in acknowledgement of Frederick Green and his family who owned land and a mill in the area and were a prominent family in the milling industry. The Dunlops were another well-known family in the area. Alexander Dunlop, who arrived here in 1821 from County Down, Ireland, owned the farm on the north east corner of Westney Road and Taunton. He died on October 21, 1870 and is buried in the Pickering United Church. A more infamous resident of South Greenwood was Oliver Badgerow. He joined William McKenzie in the Rebellion of 1837 and, in the 1840s, went on to become a member of the Markham Gang, a group of criminals who terrorized the area. He was charged with stealing a saddle in 1846 and sentenced to 7 years of hard labour. Upon his release, he settled on a 100-acre farm in what is now the southern section of Greenwood Conservation Area. He passed away in 1861 and his lonely grave can be found just southwest of the Greenwood Discovery Pavilion.

properties.NAME: Lake Vista
properties.PROFILE_2018: Prior to 1940, the community of Lake Vistas Gardens, located between Bayly Street to the north and Emperor Street to the south, was situated on farmland belonging to the Campbell family. In 1955 Regency Homes / Crusader Development Corporation Limited began construction on 500 solid brick detached and semi-detached homes which covered 71 acres of land. They celebrated their Grand Opening on March 16, 1957, offering 5 models for potential purchasers to choose from. The builder bore all of the costs for installing the services in that area including the roads, sidewalks and water mains. This was the second largest housing development to be built in Ajax after the war.
